audit_comparison.failure_modes: Garbage in: if n_candidates_compared understates how many things were really tried, the audit understates the risk.
audit_comparison.inputs: delta, n_seeds, paired, n_candidates_compared, selected_on_eval_data, confirmed_out_of_sample
audit_comparison.purpose: Grade a claimed improvement by HOW IT WAS MEASURED -- seeds, pairing, how many variants were compared, whether the winner was chosen on the data now scoring it.
audit_comparison.validation: Advisory. It grades the DESIGN of a comparison and cannot know intent, so it never blocks an experiment.
audit_comparison.when: Before believing any improvement, including your own.

capture_epoch_scores.example:
cfg['capture_epoch_scores'] = []
train_lib.train_numpy_fm(cfg, enc, splits, meta, print)
for epoch, valid_primary, scores_valid in cfg['capture_epoch_scores']:
    ...   # exactly three names, valid split only
capture_epoch_scores.failure_modes: Expecting 2 or 4 elements per entry, or expecting a (valid, test) pair inside an entry, raises at unpack time AFTER a full training run has been paid for.
capture_epoch_scores.inputs: Set cfg['capture_epoch_scores'] = [] BEFORE calling train_numpy_fm. The list is filled in place during training.
capture_epoch_scores.outputs: A LIST with one 3-tuple per epoch: (epoch:int, valid_primary:float, scores_valid:np.ndarray). VALID SPLIT ONLY -- there is no per-epoch test vector.
capture_epoch_scores.purpose: Per-epoch validation scores from the training run your script is already doing, at no extra cost.
capture_epoch_scores.validation: The per-epoch arrays are VALID-split predictions. Do not look for a test vector in them; take test predictions from train_numpy_fm's returned dict instead.
capture_epoch_scores.when: Whenever you want the epoch curve, or per-epoch predictions to feed selection_rule_test.

capture_selection_rule_test.example:
res = train_lib.train_numpy_fm(cfg, enc, splits, meta, print)
diag = capture_selection_rule_test(cfg['capture_epoch_scores'], valid_users, valid_labels)
capture_selection_rule_test.failure_modes: Requires non-empty (epoch, valid_primary, scores_valid) tuples whose score arrays match users and labels.
capture_selection_rule_test.outputs: the selection_rule_test result for best_epoch, mean_top2 and mean_top3 when enough captured epochs exist
capture_selection_rule_test.purpose: Test fixed best-epoch versus top-epoch averaging rules on held-out users using one training run's captured validation curve.
capture_selection_rule_test.validation: Diagnostic only. It does not create per-epoch test predictions and cannot itself authorise a submission change.
capture_selection_rule_test.when: After train_numpy_fm captured epoch scores and you need to check whether a checkpoint-selection rule generalises without manually rebuilding the selection_rule_test tensor and callable mapping.

ensemble_construction.failure_modes: Costs k training runs. Fewer than 4 members makes the average itself noisy.
ensemble_construction.inputs: menu_choices for the configuration, and k (number of seeds)
ensemble_construction.purpose: Train k independent seeds of one configuration, rank-normalise their predictions and average them, then score the result.
ensemble_construction.validation: Measure the gain against the MEAN member, never the best one. The best of k draws sits above the mean by construction, so that comparison reports a gain even when ensembling does nothing. Fix k before looking at any score, and use every seed trained -- dropping a weak member is selection on validation.
ensemble_construction.when: Once a configuration is CONFIRMED, or has scored repeatedly. Averaging seeds of a configuration that is not actually good just buys a precise estimate of a mediocre number.

evaluate.failure_modes: Misaligned array lengths raise; scores must be in the cache's row order.
evaluate.inputs: users: list, labels: array, scores: array
evaluate.purpose: The official metric: GAUC, nDCG@5 and their mean.
evaluate.validation: Never call this on the test split. Scoring ground truth; do not modify.
evaluate.when: To score predictions on the valid split.

free_recombination.failure_modes: Fewer members than `subset` silently shrinks the subset.
free_recombination.inputs: member_scores (members, rows), users, labels, rules: {name: fn(subset_scores) -> scores}, n_subsets, subset
free_recombination.purpose: Compare aggregation rules over stored member predictions by resampling member subsets, with no training at all.
free_recombination.validation: Requires >= 2 stored members. A rule winning on one subset is not a result; the resampled win-rate is the evidence.
free_recombination.when: When choosing how to combine models, or checking whether a combination rule that won once wins repeatedly.

get_feature_stats.purpose: Summary statistics for one cached feature column.
get_feature_stats.validation: Near-zero std can be a float artefact; compare on a scale-relative tolerance rather than testing equality.
get_feature_stats.when: To check coverage, range and missingness before using a feature.

get_label_rate_by_segment.failure_modes: Unknown feature raises KeyError; sparse bins give noisy rates.
get_label_rate_by_segment.purpose: Positive-label rate across bins of a feature.
get_label_rate_by_segment.validation: A rate difference across segments does not imply a within-user ranking gain; the metric ranks inside users, not across them.
get_label_rate_by_segment.when: When asking whether a segment of the data behaves differently.

get_user_history_stats.purpose: Distribution of per-user impression counts on a split.
get_user_history_stats.validation: Descriptive only. A difference between splits is a fact about the data, not evidence that any particular mechanism will help.
get_user_history_stats.when: When reasoning about anything that pools or weights a user's history.

get_within_user_auc.failure_modes: Unknown feature name raises KeyError. A feature with near-zero within-user variation returns an AUC near 0.5 that means 'no variation', not 'no signal'.
get_within_user_auc.purpose: AUC of a single feature computed WITHIN each user, on a chosen split.
get_within_user_auc.validation: Both metrics rank WITHIN a user, so a feature constant across a user's rows contributes nothing regardless of its global AUC.
get_within_user_auc.when: Before proposing a feature, to see whether it separates positives from negatives inside a user's own impression list.

hardcoded_constants.failure_modes: Static source scan; a constant computed at runtime is invisible to it.
hardcoded_constants.purpose: Modelling constants written into the training library, and whether each one is reachable through a pipeline override.
hardcoded_constants.validation: Reports that a constant EXISTS. It says nothing about whether changing it helps -- that requires a paired measurement.
hardcoded_constants.when: When the search keeps landing within noise and the thing that matters may be a constant no menu axis can express.

incumbent_cfg.failure_modes: Needs the loaded splits and meta. Overriding 'multitask' also rebuilds 'aux_tasks' for you.
incumbent_cfg.outputs: (cfg: dict, enc) ready to pass straight to train_numpy_fm
incumbent_cfg.purpose: Build a COMPLETE, valid training config for the incumbent, plus its feature encoding, with any key overridden by keyword.
incumbent_cfg.validation: Change ONE key per experiment. Overriding several at once makes the result uninterpretable.
incumbent_cfg.when: Before every direct call to train_numpy_fm. This is how you obtain a config; do not assemble one by hand.

pipeline_override.failure_modes: Out-of-range values are rejected with a MenuError naming the bound.
pipeline_override.inputs: one or more of: k, lr, epochs, patience, l2, bs, hist_tau_days, aux_weight, n_checkpoints, checkpoint_combine
pipeline_override.outputs: (applied to the training run; no return value)
pipeline_override.purpose: Set a training-pipeline constant the menu cannot express, by putting it directly in menu_choices.
pipeline_override.validation: Range-checked at the menu boundary. Changing several at once makes the result uninterpretable -- vary one.
pipeline_override.when: When the axis you want to change is a constant rather than a component.

selection_pressure.purpose: How large an apparent gain arises purely from picking the best of n noisy comparisons.
selection_pressure.validation: Assumes independent comparisons at the benchmark noise floor.
selection_pressure.when: Before quoting any 'we tried n things and this was best' number.

selection_rule_test.failure_modes: Passing scores for a single epoch makes the comparison meaningless; shapes must line up with users/labels.
selection_rule_test.inputs: per_epoch_scores (seeds, epochs, rows), users, labels, rules: {name: fn(per_epoch_primaries, per_epoch_scores) -> scores}
selection_rule_test.purpose: Whether a rule for CHOOSING among candidates generalises, by selecting on one half of the users and scoring on the other, in both directions, over several independent splits.
selection_rule_test.validation: Needs per-epoch predictions to already exist. The first rule in `rules` is the reference every other is measured against.
selection_rule_test.when: Whenever a number was produced by picking the best of several options on the same data it is now being scored on.

train_numpy_fm.example:
from research_tools import incumbent_cfg
cfg, enc = incumbent_cfg(splits, meta)
cfg['seed'] = args.seed
cfg['capture_epoch_scores'] = []          # optional, see below
res = train_lib.train_numpy_fm(cfg, enc, splits, meta, print)
valid_scores = res['scores_valid']        # NOT tuple unpacking
test_scores  = res['scores_test']
# cfg['capture_epoch_scores'] now holds one tuple PER EPOCH:
#     (epoch:int, valid_primary:float, scores_valid:np.ndarray)
# THREE elements, and the array is the VALID split only. There is no
# per-epoch test vector -- test scores exist only in res['scores_test'].
for epoch, valid_primary, valid_scores_at_epoch in cfg['capture_epoch_scores']:
    ...
train_numpy_fm.failure_modes: An INCOMPLETE cfg raises KeyError listing every missing key at once. An unrecognised extra key is silently ignored, so check spelling against the override list. Destructuring the return as a tuple raises ValueError.
train_numpy_fm.inputs: cfg: dict, enc, splits, meta, log: callable. The cfg must contain ALL of: dim, k, lr, bs, epochs, patience, seed, loss, history, multitask, model, training, aux_tasks. Use `cfg, enc = incumbent_cfg(splits, meta, <overrides>)` to get one. Optionally set cfg['capture_epoch_scores'] = [] first; after training that list holds (epoch, valid_primary, scores) per epoch.
train_numpy_fm.outputs: A DICT with keys: scores_valid, scores_test, model, hist. NOT a tuple -- `a, b = train_numpy_fm(...)` raises 'too many values to unpack'.
train_numpy_fm.purpose: Train one model under an explicit cfg dict and return its validation and test score vectors.
train_numpy_fm.validation: One seed is one draw. A single-seed difference is not evidence.
train_numpy_fm.when: The normal way a generated experiment produces predictions. Get the cfg from incumbent_cfg -- never hand-build it.

training_dynamics.failure_modes: Costs a full training run; allowed at most once per agent run.
training_dynamics.purpose: The validation-score curve across epochs with early stopping disabled, plus where it peaks and how far it moves afterwards.
training_dynamics.validation: The peak epoch is an argmax over many validation evaluations, so it is fitted to validation. Treat the SHAPE of the curve as the finding, not the exact peak.
training_dynamics.when: When you do not know whether the model is over- or under-fitting, and the answer would change what you try next.
